text: Writing clean code is a skill that separates good programmers from great ones. The most important rule is readability: if someone else reads your code, they should understand it easily. This means using clear naming conventions, like `calculateTotalPrice` instead of `ctp`. Avoid vague names like `data` or `temp`; instead, choose words that describe the purpose. Break your program into small, focused functions that do one thing well, rather than writing one giant block of logic. This makes testing and debugging much simpler. Ultimately, clean code improves maintainability, so you can update or fix your software months later without confusion. Remember, you are writing for humans first, and computers second.
